diagnosis: Either: Counts the starting number as the first count rather than counting the jumps backwards. Or: Counted back only two steps instead of three.
rationale: The learner said '12, 11, 10' for 12 - 3, including 12 in the count and landing on 10 instead of 9. A number line demonstrating hops backward clearly shows that the first hop lands on the number before the starting number.

script.focus: the first hop landing on 13, not 14

intent: Demonstrate subtract on the number-line with values [14,4]. Tutor points at: the first hop landing on 13, not 14

content.title: Counting back, one hop at a time

frames.caption: Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet.
Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.

judgement.reasoning: The demonstration explicitly addresses the exact misconception ('Start at 14. We are standing here; we have not hopped yet. Hop 1 moves one back and lands on 13. The first number we count is where we land, not where we started.'). It models the prerequisite counting-hop correspondence without giving away the original problem (12 - 3 vs 14 - 4), using an explicit visual demonstration.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would immediately use this worked demo because it directly targets and clarifies why the starting number is not counted as hop 1.
